newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-FIFA CHIEF WANTS PROFESSIONAL REFEREES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIFA CHIEF WANTS PROFESSIONAL REFEREES.

text.p: World soccer chief Sepp Blatter called on Sunday for professional referees to be introduced in top-class soccer and unveiled a coaching programme for officials at next year's World Cup finals in France.

"I believe totally in the idea of professional referees. Let's pay them. There is enough money," FIFA general secretary Blatter said. "There are ways to avoid a situation where people would ask how a referee could survive when his career was over.
"We should pay them when they are on duty for the national federation, confederations or FIFA. Then all this uproar about referees would come to an end."
Speaking on German television just a few days before Swiss referee Kurt Roethlisberger's appeal against a life ban for attempted bribery is heard, Blatter said he believed referees were honest.

"Referees do not swindle," he said. "In my 22 years at FIFA we have never had a case where it has been proved that a referee actively cheated. By contrast there have been players, coaches and chairmen who have been active (in that area)."
Europe's governing body UEFA banned Roethlisberger after he was found to have approached Grasshopper Zurich with an offer to fix a European Cup match, saying he knew the referee.
"Roethlisberger is not a referee anymore," Blatter said.
The consistency of refereeing at major tournaments has always been a controversial talking point.
Blatter said FIFA wanted to have a system at the 1998 World Cup where all the referees would stay together and receive coaching between matches.
"We want to have a week in March where the referees will be carefully prepared and then have another three days just before the tournament starts," Blatter said.
"During the tournament we want to keep them together in a hotel near the airport in Paris and send them out to matches from there. They will be coached there.
"Referees have to be coached as well as inspected. People forget that."
